item.title: Re: Everyone's all, "Wow, this is amazing," and then there's this asshole just sitting here like, "You forgot a comma."
item.content:encoded:
It reads like a cheesy anime fight, where the characters aren't so much fighting or outsmarting each other as asspulling secret techniques and powers, and that just doesn't do anything for me. Not much of a fan of urban fantasy style things, either, but that's personal taste and not a criticism.

This is why I upvoted. Sometimes, people don't win because they're good at what they're doing, or the good guys, or even through careful planning and good teamwork. Sometimes, people win by being high as balls, crazy as a shithouse rat, and obscenely lucky to boot. Those are the true underdog stories: the kind of people who live lives that seem less like reality and more like dipshit, goofy, ridiculous Grand Theft Auto mods. When those people win, they deserve applause simply because their victory was so damn unlikely.

I'll be going through the tale over the next few days to see where I can eliminate redundancies; I've already made most of the changes you suggested above. The only change I didn't make was with regards to the process of injecting the first demon. I had two goals for that section: make it clear that there's no magic involved in the actual drug-taking process and remove a large chunk of the thirty minute countdown to keep the pace up while still beginning with a nice fraction of time.

item.title: Everyone's all, "Wow, this is amazing," and then there's this asshole just sitting here like, "You forgot a comma."
item.content:encoded:
Gonna pick up about where I left off in chat.

The products are ready. She's not. […] The products are ready.

I think the paragraph where she ties off her arm to shoot up could be tightened up. We don't need the detailed step-by-step process - everyone knows how that goes. Could just tell us she prepares the site and the reader will fill it in.

It screeches in response; the thick dark fluid inside

Comma between "thick" and "dark." Use of "fluid" twice in this paragraph stands out to me, because the first time it's used to refer to an actual liquid, and then to describe an action. Not wrong at all, but second use is a bit unnecessary, as just describing the movement as practiced will suffice and call to mind all the same things. Similar thing with, "She shakes the syringe rapidly to reduce the gorilla back into a thick scarlet sludge." Already told us the fluid was thick, and sludge is thick, so "thick sludge" is doubly redundant. So as to not have to point out each individual instance, because I'm lazy and do not wish to build a wall that I make Recent Posts pay for, I'll just say that your descriptions can be redundant or more detailed than necessary.

Pretty sure 30 tons is a gross underestimation of how much a freight train is going to weigh. Quick Google search confirms this. Engine cars alone can weigh hundreds of tons, and with cargo you can be talking thousands.

All in all, this isn't my jam. I agree with Roget, that the main character has far too easy a time of something we're told throughout is extremely hard. It reads like a cheesy anime fight, where the characters aren't so much fighting or outsmarting each other as asspulling secret techniques and powers, and that just doesn't do anything for me. Not much of a fan of urban fantasy style things, either, but that's personal taste and not a criticism.

This helps reinforce the themes and imagery you're going for in the story. Everything works together really well writing-wise and it's highly enjoyable just to see how you put all the words together. item.title: My mama said that I'm not living right
item.content:encoded: I don't usually write stuff this fast, but Run The Jewels (specifically Oh Mama) had me wanting to snort some coke and rob a bank. Instead you get a tale written up in 26 hours about someone snorting demons and robbing a bank. Thanks to Jekeled, TyGently, and Aiden Eldritch for proofreading and fact-checking.
